text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: It costs y to take test x.
GRE(x) ::: x is the GRE test.
Provides(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is financial aid.
Applicant(x, y) ::: x is an applicant for y.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
Difficulty(x, y) ::: x is caused by y.
TooLittleMoney(x) ::: x has too little money.
TooFewResources(x) ::: x has too few resources.
Lives(x, y) ::: x lives in y.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
Dad(x, y) ::: y is the dad of x.
OutOfWork(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for y.
MoreThanAYear(y) ::: y is more than a year.
Tom(x) ::: x is Tom.
CanApply(x, y) ::: x can apply for y.
From(x, y) ::: x is from y.
ToTake(x, y) ::: x is to take y.
ETS(x) ::: x is ETS.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Money(x) ::: x is money.
Resources(x) ::: x is resources.
Premises:
Cost(GRE, 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x ∀y (Provides(ETS, FinancialAid(y), x) ∧ Applicant(x, y) ∧ Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
EconomicHardship(x) ↔ Difficulty(x, TooLittleMoney(x) ∨ TooFewResources(x)) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
Lives(Tom, SingleParentFamily(Tom)) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
∀x (SingleParentFamily(x) → ∃y (Dad(x, y) ∧ OutOfWork(y, MoreThanAYear(MoreThanAYear)))) ::: His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
CanApply(Tom, FinancialAid(GRE)) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
